name: Eternal Ltd
about: Incorporated in 2010, Eternal Limited (previously Zomato Limited) is one of the leading online Food Service platforms in terms of the value of food sold. Its offerings include food delivery, dining-out services, Loyalty programs, and others. As of December 31, 2020, Eternal has established a strong footprint across 23 countries with 131,233 active food delivery restaurants, 161,637 active delivery partners, and an average monthly food order of 10.7 million customers. [1]

flags.text: Cash conversion cycle stretched from -132 to 2 days in three years
Free cash flow negative in 4 of the last 5 years

business.what: Eternal earns from food delivery (Zomato) and quick commerce (Blinkit) in India. Blinkit's assortment is mostly first-party (1P) SKUs. Newer AI products such as dark.ai are unmonetised and sit in "Others".

segments.name: Food delivery (Zomato)
segments.comment: Competition was more intense; management is reinvesting in growth and expects margins broadly flat for 1-2 years.

segments.name: Quick commerce (Blinkit)
segments.comment: Store expansion is accelerating, mainly in smaller cities, with NOV growth expected to pick up from the December quarter.

segments.name: Others (dark.ai, enterprise AI such as Nugget)
segments.comment: Early-stage and unmonetised; costs are carved out into Others and not yet meaningful.

kpis.name: Blinkit MTU in mature cities vs Zomato MTU

ledger.promise: Consolidated margins to expand directionally, though the pace is not assured
ledger.quote: directionally we say that margin should expand, but we're not able to confidently say that the pace of margin expansion will be the same
ledger.actual: EBITDA margin rose 2.3% (Q3 FY26) → 2.8% → 2.9% → 3.1% (Q2 FY27). But the Q2 FY27 call now guides to flattish margins for the next 1-2 years.

ledger.promise: Gratuity/leave-encashment impact from new labour codes not meaningful; any impact shows in the next quarter
ledger.quote: if there is any impact, then the next quarter will reflect that, but I don't expect that to be meaningful at all.
ledger.actual: Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose to 486 from 368 and margin to 2.8% from 2.3%. PAT rose to 174 from 102. No visible hit.

ledger.promise: Going-out losses to fall sequentially toward breakeven in 4-6 quarters
ledger.quote: we now expect the losses to come down sequentially from here towards breakeven in the next four to six quarters.
ledger.actual: Deadline falls between Q3 FY27 and Q1 FY28. No segment losses are in the materials, and later calls do not report going-out losses.

ledger.promise: Going-out NOV of $3 billion by FY30 (~30% CAGR)
ledger.quote: For us to deliver 30% CAGR over the next three to four years, it doesn't necessarily mean that the industry has to grow that much.
ledger.actual: Due FY30. No segment NOV data in the materials.

ledger.promise: Net working capital not to exceed ~18 days
ledger.quote: we don't expect net working capital to be beyond those 18 days that we had shared earlier
ledger.actual: FY26 cash conversion cycle was 2 days (proxy), within 18. It has risen from -132 days (FY23) and -54 (FY25). Inventory days went from 12 to 26.

ledger.quote: the ROCE outcome should still be north of 40%. That's what we're solving for.
ledger.actual: No capital-employed or segment ROCE data in the materials, and later calls do not report ROCE.

ledger.promise: Food delivery YoY growth to trend up slowly toward 20%
ledger.quote: we expect year-on-year growth to continue slowly trending up towards 20% YoY, is what our current sense on the market is.
ledger.actual: No food delivery segment data. The Q1 FY27 call cites an LPG-related impact that took some restaurants offline.

ledger.promise: 3,000 quick commerce dark stores by March
ledger.quote: On store addition, we're on track on our guidance for March of 3,000 stores. We remain firmly on track.
ledger.actual: The call was held in May 2026, so it is unclear which March is meant. No store count is reported. Q2 FY27 says store additions accelerate from OND.

ledger.promise: Quick commerce NOV/GOV 60% CAGR over three years
ledger.quote: what we have done here is actually given a more longer term three-year guidance.
ledger.actual: Three-year horizon not reached. No segment NOV is given. Consolidated revenue in Q2 FY27 was 24,138 vs 13,590 a year earlier (+77.6%), but the 1P shift distorts the comparison.

ledger.promise: Quick commerce contribution margin of 5-6% at some point; raised to the top of the range (~6%) in Q1 FY27
ledger.quote: As we move to 5-6% margin that we are saying we will get to at some point, contribution margin will go up
ledger.actual: No date given and no segment margin data. Q1 FY27 raised the target to the higher end. Q2 FY27 says store acceleration will not hurt margins in the short term.

ledger.quote: We maintain that guidance as of now.
ledger.actual: Due FY29. TTM reported EBITDA is 2,200 crore. 'Adjusted EBITDA' is not defined in the materials.

ledger.promise: About 90-95% 1P mix reached; no further incremental working-capital change on that account
ledger.quote: we are at that steady state now where about 90-95% is 1P, and we don't expect any more incremental working capital change on that account
ledger.actual: FY27 working-capital days not yet available. Borrowings rose to 5,757 (FY27) from 4,592 (FY26).

current_guidance.quote: broadly, over the next 1 or 2 years, we expect the margins to remain flattish.
We maintain that guidance as of now.

current_guidance.metric: Quick commerce margin during accelerated store addition
current_guidance.target: No short-term margin hit; margins keep expanding longer term
current_guidance.quote: as we accelerate store addition, which is starting OND, we don't expect that to hit the margins in the short term. Longer term, of course, margins will continue expanding
we think at this point we're likely to end at the higher end of the range that we had guided earlier
We are fairly comfortable and confident that over a period of three years, we should be able to deliver this CAGR of growth.
We gave guidance last time that in steady state it could get to about INR 11 lakh per day per store. We are at INR 9 lakh today.
we don't expect any more incremental working capital change on that account

current_guidance.target: Bulk of new stores in smaller cities
current_guidance.quote: the bulk of the expansion of these new stores will be in smaller cities. We do expect that to be the focus from here on
we don't expect the capex or cost to become meaningful, at least as of now, unless, of course, we receive a blockbuster response to this product.

credibility.label: mixed
credibility.summary: The few near-term promises that can be checked held up: margins rose every quarter after the Q3 FY26 call, the labour-code cost did not dent Q4 FY26, and the working-capital proxy stayed within 18 days. Against that, the Q2 FY27 call cut the margin outlook from 'expand' to 'flattish for 1-2 years', and most of the promises that matter for valuation (QC 60% CAGR, going-out breakeven, $1bn FY29 EBITDA, ROCE >40%) are either not yet due or cannot be checked with the data provided.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Margin expansion pace uncertain due to high competitive intensity; near-term margins unpredictable
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: EBITDA margin rose each quarter: 2.3% (Q3 FY26), 2.8%, 2.9%, 3.1% (Q2 FY27). EBITDA went from 368 to 752.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Margins flattish for 1-2 years, yet the $1bn Adjusted EBITDA target for FY29 is maintained
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: TTM EBITDA is 2,200 on revenue of 77,956 (2.8%). With flat margins, the target depends almost entirely on revenue growth. Adjusted EBITDA is not reconciled in the materials.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Operating progress framed through EBITDA/contribution margin expansion
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: PAT has not followed EBITDA. FY26 PAT was 366 vs 527 in FY25 while EBITDA rose from 637 to 1,208. Q1 FY27 PAT was 92 vs 174 in Q4 FY26 despite EBITDA rising from 486 to 594.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Working capital contained at ≤18 days and the 1P shift now at steady state
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: Cash conversion cycle went from -132 days (FY23) to -54 (FY25) to +2 (FY26). Inventory days went from 11 (FY24) to 26 (FY26). Borrowings rose from 749 (FY24) to 5,757 (FY27). Within the cap, but the negative working-capital float is gone.

bull.point: Margins and EBITDA have improved every quarter for six quarters
bull.evidence: EBITDA margin went from 1.6% (Q1 FY26) to 3.1% (Q2 FY27). EBITDA went from 115 to 752.
Q2 FY27 revenue was 24,138 vs 13,590 in Q2 FY26 (+77.6%). TTM revenue is 77,956 vs FY26's 54,364. The 1P shift inflates part of this.

bull.point: Quick commerce margin target raised, and store acceleration is not expected to hurt near-term margins
bull.evidence: Likely to end at the higher end of the 5-6% range. Accelerating store addition from OND is not expected to hit margins in the short term.
bull.source: Q1 FY27 call p3; Q2 FY27 call p8

bear.point: Margin outlook cut to flattish while competition and discounting continue
bear.evidence: 'over the next 1 or 2 years, we expect the margins to remain flattish'. Earlier, competition was said to hurt margins, growth and store plans, and current discounting was called unsustainable.
bear.source: Q2 FY27 call p3; Q3 FY26 call p5; Q1 FY27 call p5

bear.point: Bottom line is thin and has not tracked EBITDA
bear.evidence: TTM PAT is 493 on revenue of 77,956 (~0.6%). FY26 PAT of 366 was below FY25's 527. Q1 FY27 PAT of 92 was below Q4 FY26's 174.

bear.point: Balance sheet is absorbing the shift to an inventory-led model
bear.evidence: Cash conversion cycle went from -132 days (FY23) to +2 (FY26). Borrowings rose from 749 to 5,757 and CWIP from 136 to 296. Management expects capex per store to rise.
bear.source: reported numbers; Q3 FY26 call p6

call.credential: Category Head, Blinkit at Eternal (Zomato, Blinkit), 2021–2024
call.knows: the demand and channel reality behind the quarter
